examples.title: Rudzik
examples.motion: The robin crouches, rises into a short song with an open beak, and settles.
sequence: Right-facing resting robin, beak closed, feet planted at original positions, tail extending to the left.

Peak short song: clearly open beak, higher head and full rounded chest, tail dipped for counterbalance; both feet remain planted.
Release: beak closes, head lowers, chest relaxes and body begins to sink back.
Settles near the original posture with a subtle remaining head lift and tail lower than at stage one; do not duplicate first stage.

examples.title: Sroka
examples.motion: The magpie draws back, bows to peck its original trunk, then lifts its head and settles its tail.
sequence: Original right-facing magpie on a complete pale trunk with its connected oak sprig, head bowed, full long tail extending down-left.
Anticipation: head draws back and slightly up, chest lifts and neck shortens; feet grip the same trunk and tail lowers a little.
Approach: bird bows its head downward and slightly back toward the existing bark immediately ABOVE ITS OWN FEET; neck curves, torso leans gently and tail lifts modestly.

Peak single peck: closed beak points DOWN and slightly inward, its tip visibly touching the SAME central trunk surface immediately above its feet. Head is lower, neck flexed, tail lifted in counterbalance. The trunk stays intact, same shape, same location.
Release: beak lifts off that same patch of central trunk, neck begins to unfold and tail begins to lower.
Settles nearly to initial bowed-head pose with a slightly different head angle, full tail again down-left. Distinct from first stage.
